agent.problem: This non-opening story card runs for four sentences, including the Elkanah joke and the detail about Samuel's sons. It exceeds the one-to-two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: Too many choices depend on information that cannot be reasoned out from the earlier cards. Card 5's timing, card 6's tabernacle, card 7's regulations and card 9's scope of service have not been supplied or made inferable. That makes four of the seven choices discovery questions, with cards 7 and 9 effectively coin flips, so most choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The blank asks for the unseen verse's wording, but no earlier card has mentioned the tabernacle or established the pre-temple setting. The baker cannot reason out why tabernacle, rather than palace or throne, belongs in the blank.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

human.problem: Cards 11 and 13 ask where Asaph stands (at Heman's right hand) and where the Merarites stand (on the left). Both details sit inside the singers' family lines (6:39-47). They could count as part of a genealogy, which is a long stretch, or as a description of how the music ministry was arranged.
human.question: When the singers' positions (right hand, left) are given inside their family lines, do they belong to the genealogy long stretch, so no choice cards? Or are they part of the service description and allowed to be asked?
